main_body: Flat ground/paving patch of dark grey-brown cobble/scale tiles repeating across the whole 4x3 tile area; terrain tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none: terrain pattern, no standing body. A column read shows repeating small light-grey cobble highlights over mid and dark grey-brown rows.
evidence: The candidate is a seamless ground paving texture, not a standing object. The 3/4 contract of top band plus front face does not apply to terrain. No side faces, no elevation drawing. Nothing in it violates the terrain kind.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 5 lightness steps, from near-black joints through mid grey-brown to a light grey-tan highlight on each cobble crest. The joints are dark with a slight brown-purple lean, so they read as material tone rather than neutral black. The pattern is a very regular repeat of identical cobble clusters, with the same highlight blob on every row and little per-stone variation. The paving reference has varied stones with edge highlights, slab seams and speckle, so this reads more mechanical and slightly less rich. It has no large flat fills, since every area has tonal stepping. Overall it is acceptable next to the reference, though a bit uniform and lower in per-tile variation.
